n this chapter we begin a radical departure from the emphasis on the single mol e cule that permeates the previous twenty chapters. Unit II describes the chemical bonding and structure of single, isolated mol e cules. Unit III explains the macroscopic properties of gases and liquids through intermo lec u lar forces that originate in the structures of individual mol e cules. While the behavior of many mol e cules contributes to these properties, the mechanism of their contribution is essentially that a few mol e cules come close enough to a “target” mol e cule to expe- rience the intermo lec u lar forces it sets up. Units IV and V deal with the equilibrium and rate aspects of chemical reactions as consequences of collisions between indi- vidual mol e cules.
